prompt: What does `pl render` do?

choices.text: Calls the model once and prints its reply to the first case of the set
choices.why: That would be a run; render makes no call.

choices.text: Fills a template's holes and prints the result
choices.why: Right: the prompt the model would be sent.

choices.text: Checks the replies of a run
choices.why: That is `pl check`.

choices.text: Counts the tokens in a prompt file and prices each call
choices.why: That is `pl tokens` and `pl cost`.

prompt: `pl render` was given no value for `{{language}}`. With what exit status did it stop?
Why keep one reply template with `{{shop}}` and `{{language}}` rather than a copy of the prompt for each shop and language?

choices.text: An instruction then lives in one file, so a fix is made once and is not forgotten in a copy
choices.why: Right: one place to change.

choices.text: Templates run faster
choices.why: The model reads the filled prompt either way.

choices.text: Copies cost more tokens
choices.why: Each call sends one prompt either way.

choices.text: Models refuse copied prompts
choices.why: A model cannot tell.

prompt: When `pl run` calls the model, what does the model read?
hint: The holes are not sent as holes.

choices.text: The template, holes included, with the values sent separately beside it
choices.why: The values are pasted in before the call.

choices.text: The file in `prompts/` exactly as written
choices.why: That still has its holes.

choices.text: Only the values passed with `--var`
choices.why: It reads the instructions too.

choices.text: The filled template
choices.why: Right: what render prints.

prompt: By default, what does Jinja2 render in place of an undefined variable?

choices.text: An error that stops the render
choices.why: That is what `pl render` does; Jinja2's default does not.

choices.text: The placeholder as written
choices.why: That is `string.Template` with `safe_substitute`.

choices.text: The word *undefined*
choices.why: It writes nothing at all.

choices.text: An empty string
choices.why: Right, and the prompt goes out with a hole in its sentence.

prompt: Why must a missing value stop the run rather than render as empty?

choices.text: Because the model then answers with an error message instead of a reply whenever a placeholder is blank
choices.why: It answers something plausible, which is the problem.

choices.text: Nothing after the render is able to tell an empty hole from a short sentence
choices.why: Right: the defect would ship silently.

choices.text: It saves tokens
choices.why: A few tokens are not the issue.

choices.text: The stand-in crashes
choices.why: It would answer; that is the danger.

prompt: Somebody runs the reply template with `--var tone=warm`, and the template has no `{{tone}}`. What happened?
hint: Where would the value have gone?

choices.text: The replies got warmer, as the person who read them noticed
choices.why: The value had nowhere to go; the warmth is in the reading.

choices.text: The harness added a tone line to the end of the prompt by itself
choices.why: It pastes values into holes and nowhere else.

choices.text: The value never reached the model
choices.why: Right, and the warning is the only sign.

choices.text: The run failed
choices.why: The prompt rendered correctly.

prompt: Why render one case before running a template you have just changed?
hint: Compare what `pl run` and `pl render` print.

choices.text: `pl run` does not repeat the warnings per case, so the render is where an unused value shows
choices.why: Right, and it costs no call.

choices.text: Rendering trains the model on the template
choices.why: Nothing is trained.

choices.text: A run refuses to start without one
choices.why: It starts; it just stays quiet about unused values.

choices.text: To warm up the cache
choices.why: Render makes no call, so it touches no cache.

prompt: A template is edited and `{{tone}}` becomes `{{register}}`. A script that still passes `tone` now gets a warning that the value is ___.
Why did case `a08` break the structure of `v5-tagged.txt`?

choices.text: Its text contains `</message>`, which closes the tag the template opened, so the next line falls outside
choices.why: Right: a value that ends its own hole.

choices.text: It is too long
choices.why: It is three short lines.

choices.text: It is in another language
choices.why: It is in English.

choices.text: It has no category
choices.why: Its expected category is delivery.

prompt: What does the `|xml` filter change?
hint: Look at `<` in the rendered prompt.

choices.text: It wraps the entire template, instructions included, in XML so the model reads each line as data
choices.why: It touches the value only; the instructions stay instructions.

choices.text: It replaces `<`, `>` and `&` in the value with XML entities
choices.why: Right: the customer's tag stops closing anything.

choices.text: It deletes the tags
choices.why: The customer's words are all still there.

choices.text: It parses the reply
choices.why: It acts on the prompt, before the call.

prompt: Why is the filter applied to the value and not to the whole template?

choices.text: Applying it to the whole template would make the prompt too long for the model to read
choices.why: Length is not the issue; the template's tags would stop being tags.

choices.text: The template is escaped already when it is saved under `prompts/`
choices.why: Nothing escapes it; it holds real tags on purpose.

choices.text: Filters work only on values read from a JSON file
choices.why: A `--var` value is filtered the same way.

choices.text: The template's own tags stay tags
choices.why: Right: only text from outside is changed.

prompt: Which of these values should be escaped before they are pasted between the template's tags? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A customer's message
choices.why: Yes: a customer can type a closing tag.

choices.text: Text copied from a web form
choices.why: Yes: it came from outside.

choices.text: A book review a customer wrote
choices.why: Yes, for the same reason.

choices.text: The shop name you chose for `{{shop}}`
choices.why: You wrote it; it holds no tag unless you put one there.

prompt: Why does a test set need one template rendered the same way for every case?

choices.text: Because the harness is unable to open more than one prompt file in the same directory at once
choices.why: It opens whichever file you name.

choices.text: So that each message gets the same answer from the model
choices.why: The answers differ; the instructions do not.

choices.text: So a difference between runs is the template's doing
choices.why: Right: only the message changes from case to case.

choices.text: To save disk space
choices.why: Space has nothing to do with it.

prompt: What is the prompt id that `pl run` prints?

choices.text: A counter that goes up by one each time a prompt in the lab runs, kept in a hidden file
choices.why: Two runs of one file printed the same id.

choices.text: The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the prompt file
choices.why: Right: `b04095b1` both ways.

choices.text: The date of the last edit
choices.why: It is a hash of the content.

choices.text: A random name for the run
choices.why: It is the same every time the file is the same.

prompt: Two runs of `v17-static-first.txt` both print `prompt b04095b1`, and one used `--set temperature=0.8`. Why is that a problem?

choices.text: The id covers the file and not the command line, so the run files make the two look like one prompt
choices.why: Right: keep settings in the header, where the id sees them.

choices.text: The second run overwrote the first
choices.why: They were written to different files.

choices.text: The hash is broken
choices.why: It hashed the same file twice, correctly.

choices.text: Temperature has no effect
choices.why: It does; the id just does not record it.

prompt: In this lab a prompt file carries its settings as `name: value` lines above a line of three ___.
Put the steps of putting a changed template to use in order.
items: Write the template with named holes
Render one case and read the result
Fix what the render reports as missing or unused
Run it over the test set

prompt: Match each message from the harness to what it means.

pairs.right: A value that ends its own hole

right_distractors: A reply that does not parse

prompt: Replies that should be in Portuguese started arriving in English yesterday. The template says `Write in {{language}}.`, and your engine renders a missing value as an empty string. What do you check first?
hint: What would the model have read?

choices.text: Whether the model was retrained on English material since the day before yesterday
choices.why: Look at what you sent before suspecting the model.

choices.text: Whether the test set has enough Portuguese messages in it to measure
choices.why: Useful later; the symptom points at the render.

choices.text: Whether the language value is still passed
choices.why: Right: an empty hole reads as *Write in .*

choices.text: The temperature
choices.why: Temperature does not choose a language.
